```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```


```{python}
# import your data here using polars and the URL
import pandas as pd

url = "https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/raw/master/data-raw/dwellings_ml/dwellings_ml.csv"
df = pl.from_pandas(pd.read_csv(url))

features = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ("yrbuilt", "before1980", "parcel")]
X = df.select(features).to_numpy()
y = df["before1980"].to_numpy()

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Repeat the classification exercise using 2 different algorithms/models. Explain the differences between the 3 models__ (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task).

A Decision Tree splits on one feature at a time and is simple but prone to overfitting. Random Forest fixes this by averaging hundreds of trees trained on random data subsets, reducing variance. Gradient Boosting builds trees sequentially, each correcting the last. Which typically yields the highest accuracy of the three.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
dt = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=10, random_state=42)
dt.fit(X_train, y_train)

rf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=10, random_state=42)
rf.fit(X_train, y_train)

gb = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=42)
gb.fit(X_train, y_train)

for name, model in [("Decision Tree", dt), ("Random Forest", rf), ("Gradient Boosting", gb)]:
    acc = metrics.accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
    print(f"{name}: {acc:.4f}")
```


## QUESTION 2

1. For each model (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task), display the classification report and the permutation importances for the most important features.  Discuss which model you would recommend to the Client and why.

The Decision Tree had the weakest F1 score on the pre-1980 class. Random Forest improved significantly, and Gradient Boosting achieved the best accuracy and F1 balance overall. Across all three models, livearea, basement, and stories ranked as the most important features. Gradient Boosting is recommended. It best identifies pre-1980 homes, which is the highest-stakes prediction given the asbestos risk.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
feature_names = features

for name, model in [("Decision Tree", dt), ("Random Forest", rf), ("Gradient Boosting", gb)]:
    print(f"\n{'='*50}")
    print(f"  {name}")
    print('='*50)
    
    # Classification report
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    print(metrics.classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=["Post-1980", "Pre-1980"]))
    
    # Permutation importance
    perm = permutation_importance(model, X_test, y_test, n_repeats=10, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
    imp_df = (
        pl.DataFrame({"feature": feature_names, "importance": perm.importances_mean})
        .sort("importance", descending=True)
        .head(10)
    )
    print("Top 10 features by permutation importance:")
    print(imp_df)
```
